description: This bar chart, from the paper “Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces,” illustrates the GLUE Performance for different fine-tuning methods when applied to two variants of the RoBERTa model: “base” (represented by blue bars) and “large” (represented by orange bars). The horizontal axis, labeled “Fine-tuning Method,” lists the methods in the following order: Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, S₄-model, and S₅-model. The vertical axis, labeled “GLUE Performance,” is scaled linearly from approximately 85 to 89, with major tick marks at 86 and 88. For each fine-tuning method, two bars are shown side-by-side, with the “base” model bar appearing to the left and the “large” model bar to the right. The “large” model consistently achieves higher performance than the “base” model across all methods, with the most significant performance difference observed in the LoRA method (88.0 for large vs. 87.0 for base) and the smallest difference in the BitFit method (85.0 for base vs. 85.5 for large). The chart does not show any sorting of the bars by performance, and all bars are presented with uniform width and solid fill, with no visual emphasis or annotations beyond the color-coded legend.
